quizzes.title: Checkpoint 1 — Process, Frames, and Hierarchy
quizzes.intro: Check design process basics, file structure, and visual hierarchy before components.

questions.prompt: What should you clarify before polishing visual decoration?

options.text: The exact shadow blur for every card
The user goal, primary action, essential content, and constraints
How many gradients fit above the fold
Which stock illustration pack is trendiest

questions.explanation: Structure and intent come before decoration; otherwise polish hides confusion.

wrongExplanations.a: Effects are secondary to task clarity.
wrongExplanations.c: Gradient count is not a foundation decision.
wrongExplanations.d: Trends do not define the job of the screen.

options.text: To force stakeholders to debate corner radius immediately
To focus critique on structure and flow before visual styling distracts
Because Figma cannot create high-fidelity screens
Because color is forbidden in all final products

questions.explanation: Unfinished looks help people evaluate layout and intent instead of aesthetics.

wrongExplanations.a: Early reviews should avoid skin-deep debates.
wrongExplanations.c: Figma supports high fidelity; sequencing is the point.
wrongExplanations.d: Color comes later; it is not permanently forbidden.

questions.prompt: Why rename frames and layers carefully?

options.text: Because Figma deletes unnamed layers nightly
Because clear names make collaboration, search, and handoff usable
Because names change the compiled binary of the app automatically
Because prototypes require random names

questions.explanation: A tree full of Rectangle 24 becomes unusable quickly for teams and future you.

wrongExplanations.a: Figma does not auto-delete unnamed layers on a nightly schedule.
wrongExplanations.c: Layer names do not compile your production app by themselves.
wrongExplanations.d: Prototypes benefit from clear, not random, names.

questions.prompt: Which practice best establishes visual hierarchy?

options.text: Using size, weight, contrast, spacing, and position intentionally
Making every element the same size and contrast
Using as many fonts as possible
Relying only on random bright colors

questions.explanation: Hierarchy is created by controlled differences that guide the eye to what matters.

wrongExplanations.c: Too many fonts create noise, not clarity.
wrongExplanations.d: Color alone without structure is unreliable and often inaccessible.

questions.prompt: Why design empty and error states early?

options.text: Because happy-path screens never ship
Because real products spend time in incomplete and failure conditions that beginners often omit
Because Figma requires exactly three error modals
Because empty states replace navigation permanently

questions.explanation: Flows break in real use when only ideal filled states are designed.

wrongExplanations.a: Happy paths do ship; they are incomplete alone.
wrongExplanations.c: There is no fixed mandatory modal count.
wrongExplanations.d: Empty states complement, not replace, navigation.

quizzes.title: Checkpoint 2 — Auto Layout, Components, and Styles
quizzes.intro: Test reusable structure and layout systems in Figma.

questions.prompt: What is auto layout mainly for?

options.text: Arranging child elements by direction, gap, and padding so UI adapts more predictably
Exporting videos only
Deleting components automatically
Turning off all constraints forever

questions.explanation: Auto layout creates structured, adaptable frames for buttons, lists, cards, and more.

wrongExplanations.b: Auto layout is about structure, not video export.
wrongExplanations.c: It does not exist to delete components.
wrongExplanations.d: It improves layout control rather than removing it.

questions.prompt: What is the benefit of components?

options.text: They prevent any design from being reused
You build once, reuse instances, and update the source to propagate changes
They force you to detach everything immediately
They replace the need for typography

questions.explanation: Components create reusable, maintainable UI building blocks.

wrongExplanations.a: Reuse is the point of components.

options.text: Grouping related component states such as primary/secondary or default/disabled
Randomly renaming pages at midnight
Measuring CPU temperature
Hiding all comments

questions.explanation: Variants package related states into one configurable component set.

wrongExplanations.b: Variants are design-system structure, not page-renaming automation.
wrongExplanations.c: Hardware metrics are outside Figma variants.
wrongExplanations.d: Comment visibility is a collaboration setting, not a variant purpose.

questions.prompt: Why create text and color styles even on small projects?

options.text: Because styles make inconsistency mandatory
Because named reusable definitions prevent drift and make global updates easier
Because Figma bans local colors otherwise
Because styles replace frames

questions.explanation: Styles keep visual decisions consistent and maintainable as files grow.

wrongExplanations.c: Local colors are possible; styles are recommended judgment.

questions.prompt: Which resizing idea is important in auto layout?

options.text: Hug contents, fill container, and fixed sizes as intentional choices
Only fixed sizes forever with no exceptions
Never use padding
Always overlap children randomly

questions.explanation: Choosing hug/fill/fixed correctly is central to adaptable components.

wrongExplanations.b: Rigid fixed sizing fights responsive UI needs.
wrongExplanations.c: Padding is a core auto layout control.

quizzes.title: Final Quiz — Prototypes, Handoff, and Accessibility
quizzes.intro: Apply interaction design, collaboration, and quality judgment.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of an early click-through prototype?

options.text: To impress with maximum animation on every element
To learn whether people can understand and complete the flow
To replace usability testing forever
To avoid designing error paths

questions.explanation: Prototypes are learning tools for flow clarity, not decoration contests.

wrongExplanations.a: Motion should support orientation, not create noise.
wrongExplanations.c: Prototypes support testing; they do not obsolete it.

questions.prompt: Which handoff practice helps developers most?

options.text: Deliver only one happy-path screenshot with unnamed layers
Provide named components, key states, spacing/type clarity, and notes on unfinished areas
Hide responsive behavior on purpose
Detach every component before sharing

questions.explanation: Implementable design includes states, names, and explicit gaps—not mystery polish.

wrongExplanations.a: Missing states and names create rework.

questions.prompt: Which accessibility habit belongs in foundation UI design?

options.text: Rely on color alone for all meaning
Ensure sufficient text contrast and visible focus states
Use placeholder-only labeling with no field labels
Make mobile touch targets as tiny as possible

questions.explanation: Contrast and focus visibility are baseline accessible design requirements.

wrongExplanations.d: Tiny targets harm mobile usability and accessibility.

questions.prompt: How should you ask for design feedback?

options.text: Only say "Thoughts?" with no context
State the user goal and ask a specific question about hierarchy or clarity
Forbid comments on the file
Request feedback only after development ships

questions.explanation: Specific, goal-framed questions produce actionable critique.

wrongExplanations.c: Comments are a core collaboration channel.
wrongExplanations.d: Feedback is most valuable before expensive implementation.

options.text: Because detached instances stay perfectly synced forever
Because detaching breaks the update/propagation benefits of a design system
Because Figma deletes detached layers instantly
Because variants cannot exist otherwise

questions.explanation: Systems work when instances remain connected to maintainable sources.

wrongExplanations.a: Detached elements no longer inherit source updates.
wrongExplanations.d: Variants exist independently of detaching habits.

questions.prompt: A screen looks polished but users cannot find the next step in a prototype test. What should you do?

options.text: Add more shadows and declare victory
Revisit hierarchy, labeling, and flow structure before more decoration
Ignore the test because aesthetics are enough
Convert all text to light gray icons only

questions.explanation: If the flow fails, polish is irrelevant until structure and clarity are fixed.

wrongExplanations.a: Effects do not solve wayfinding failures.
wrongExplanations.c: User confusion is a design signal, not noise.
wrongExplanations.d: Removing readable text usually worsens comprehension.
